title: Mendoza: Mary may receive latria by contact with Christ—secondary and respective, if scandal is avoided (Cajetan on Thomas)
source_text: XXXVII. Caeterum quamvis Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae adorationem qua Sancti coluntur, non ad Latriam, verum ad Duliam pertinere doceant, quam vero Beatae Virgini deferunt, ad Hyperduliam; nihilominus nonnulli eorum in quaestionem vocant, an non etiam Latria Virgo Maria possit adorari? Et ad quaestionem illam affirmative Respondent. Id praesertim videre est apud Franciscum Mendoza Jesuitam. Proposita enim ista quaestione, Utrum Beata Virgo adoratione Latriae adorari queat? Ad eam solvendam notat tria dignitatis genera in Virgine observari posse. Prima dignitas consistit in illius sanctitate, ob quam adoratione Duliae colendam esse dicit. Secunda in eo quod est mater Dei, propter quam Hyperduliae cultu adorandam esse statuit. Tertia in eo quod tetigit Christum Dominum nostrum, ratione cujus existimat Virginem adoratione Latriae coli posse. Sicut, ex sententia Thomae, crux, & clavi, aliaque quae Christi corpus tetigerunt, Latriae cultu colenda sunt. Postquam enim sibi multa in contrarium opposuit, quaestionem sic tandem concludit, Nihilominus dicendum est posse Beatam Virginem ratione solius contactus adorari adoratione Latriae. Neque divus Thomas absolute hoc negat, sed quando est scandalum aut periculum Idololatriae, ut ejus interpres Cajetanus exponit. Quare si quis idoneus sit ad discernendas rationes adorationis, & cavendum omne scandalum, poterat Beatam Virginem ratione contactus adorare adoratione Latriae: quamvis enim haec adoratio Latriae non sit primaria & absoluta, est tamen secundaria & respectiva, ab uno eodemque habitu Religionis proficiscens. In Virid. lib. 2. de Floribus sacris problem. 4. Ut refertur apud Carolum Drelincurtium de honore Beatae Virgini debito Tom. 1. pag. 355.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover although the Doctors of the Roman Church teach that the adoration by which the Saints are cultivated pertains not to Latria but to Dulia, but that which they render to the Blessed Virgin to Hyperdulia; nevertheless some of them call into question whether the Virgin Mary cannot also be adored with Latria. And to that question they Answer affirmatively. That is especially to be seen in Francis Mendoza the Jesuit. For when that question is proposed, Whether the Blessed Virgin can be adored with the adoration of Latria? To solve it he notes that three genera of dignity can be observed in the Virgin. The first dignity consists in her sanctity, for which he says she is to be cultivated with the adoration of Dulia. The second in that she is mother of God, for which he lays down that she is to be adored with the cult of Hyperdulia. The third in that she touched Christ our Lord, by reason of which he judges the Virgin can be cultivated with the adoration of Latria. Just as, by Thomas’s sentence, the cross, and nails, and other things which touched Christ’s body, are to be cultivated with the cult of Latria. For after he opposed many things to himself to the contrary, he at last concludes the question thus: Nevertheless it is to be said that the Blessed Virgin can be adored with the adoration of Latria by reason of contact alone. Nor does holy Thomas absolutely deny this, but when there is scandal or danger of Idolatry, as his interpreter Cajetan explains. Wherefore if anyone is fit to discern the reasons of adoration and to avoid all scandal, he could adore the Blessed Virgin with the adoration of Latria by reason of contact: for although this adoration of Latria is not primary and absolute, yet it is secondary and respective, proceeding from one and the same habit of Religion. In the Viridarium, book 2, on Sacred Flowers, problem 4. As is reported in Charles Drelincourt On the honor owed to the Blessed Virgin, volume 1, page 355.
pass_b_english: School baseline: Saints get dulia, Mary hyperdulia—yet Mendoza asks if she may also take latria.
Three dignities: holiness (dulia), maternity (hyperdulia), contact with Christ (latria), as cross and nails do.
Cajetan’s Thomas: allowed as secondary respective latria if scandal is kept off—so Mendoza concludes.
